nodes.name: The long game
nodes.is: Everything the product offers a person over months. Each pass is a stretch of sittings that ends because the world, the fleet or the meta changed.

phases.d: Something pulled you in: a friend, news from the sea, a new hull, habit.
Home offers the Toybox, the Arcade, the Arena and Voyages.
Rounds in one place, sometimes crossing to another.
Crystals, quest progress, artifacts, standing, replays.
Spend and arrange: a vessel, a squad, a pilot, an artifact.
The sea ticks, sagas open, the meta is rebalanced, a vessel is added.

now.note: The places and most arcs exist. Nothing in the build changes on a schedule, so the last phase is empty today.

plan.note: The meta is rebalanced on a schedule by the elemental loop's step 5, voyages add a living sea with sagas and relics, and new vessels enter at step 1 and unsettle more than their own balance.

prop.note: Give the last phase a name and a clock: the Tide (see The Tide).

holes.q: How often a person comes back is now read (the Froglet Analytics console's Sessions and Retention pages, from session_started and session_ended in builds after 2026-11-07; PostHog was closed on 2026-11-23), but how many sittings make one pass is not, because nothing marks a pass or a Tide.
holes.fill: Target 3 to 5 sittings a week and one Tide every 6 weeks. Read sittings per week from the Sessions page's sessions per player, and mark the pass with a tide_started event when the Tide ships, before tuning anything above the Round.

holes.fill: The breath (new loop): after each result, one offered next step chosen from what the round just trained.

holes.q: Rounds per sitting and places per sitting are not measured. Sessions are (session_started, session_ended), but game_started does not carry their session_id (Docs/Analytics/EVENT_SCHEMA.json), so a round cannot be put in its sitting except by time.
holes.fill: Aim for 5 to 8 rounds and 1 or 2 places in a sitting. Add session_id to game_started (Froglet Analytics only, as session_ended does) and count rounds and places per session on the Sessions page.

holes.q: The Session tier starts at 10 minutes, but a commuter's and a casual phone player's sittings are 4 to 8 minutes. Rounds fit them (94 to 100% of sittings); a voyage fits 0 to 1% of them as planned and 14 to 21% as built.
holes.fill: A sitting may be one round. The breath (P5) offers 'one more' or 'your daily job is waiting', and a voyage can be left at a location and picked up next sitting (P13).

nodes.name: Toybox
nodes.is: Freestyle. Nothing is scored. You fly, find toys and try hulls. It is also the menu's background, so every sitting starts inside it.

holes.q: What a toy session is for, in loop terms, is not written: there is no stated reason to leave a toy or to come back to one.
holes.fill: A toy's exit is a crossing. Every toy names the scored loop it is the free version of, and offers it when the player has done the toy's verb a few times.

holes.q: The Toybox pays no progress. A player who only paints earns about 100 crystals in six weeks (simulated), so the long game never starts for them.
holes.fill: P16: a finished painting pays a little and can be shared as a replay link (P12), and a liked painting is the creative player's 'I won'.

holes.q: Every arc in the atlas is fed by winning. A player who only makes things (the painter in Docs/LoopAtlas/personas/journeys.yaml) moves no arc, and has seen every painting and microscene by week 3.
holes.fill: Each week of the Tide adds one painting and one microscene, and a shared painting opens the same canvas for whoever taps it.

The card seats its hull.
I1 intro, I2 fun, I3 challenging, I4 very hard.
Aimed at about 90 seconds for an experienced pilot.
Placing and the payout.

nodes.is: A card's four rungs. Each rung adds one demand to the one below, coupled to the game's element the same way on every card.

plan.note: One human plays the four rungs and signs them off as fun; only then is that vessel and element sent to AI training.

holes.q: Nothing checks that the rungs are four steps for the fixed AI. Grizzly Time's AI (fb750ac38, GRIZZLYTIME.md, 24 courses) finishes I1 70 s, I2 72, I3 82, I4 83: the rungs come out as two pairs, so I2's level-5 start and I4's fauna add almost nothing for it.
holes.fill: Judge each card's ladder by the fixed AI's time per rung (regatta_judge) and flag two neighbouring rungs closer than about 5% as a ladder to retune before step 3 signs off.

nodes.name: A voyage
nodes.is: The culminating experience. A squad of three and one Ark sail the shared HyperSea from port to places and home again. What is aboard when you dock is yours.

phases.d: Your pilots drum up jobs for their factions.
Flown with the Ark, cell after cell.
The location's experience.

now.note: V1 is built as the slice and D1 deepens it on the device: the living galaxy, rival crews by the same rules, work verbs, sagas, standing. Run once in Unity by Garrett. The networked Ark, rival Arks in the world and meeting other squads are not built.

plan.note: V2 to V4: squads meet on arrival, placed by galactic traffic control so the meeting makes sense to both sides' missions. 3 to 6 legs, 20 to 40 minutes.

prop.note: Docking offers the Hangar when the pay covers a vessel, and the next saga chapter when one opened.

holes.q: It is not said whether voyage pay is the same crystals that buy vessels, so the step from 'voyage ends' to 'spend it on a vessel' has no confirmed path.
holes.fill: One soft currency. Voyage pay is crystals, paid at dock, scaled so a clean voyage is worth about three arcade wins.

holes.q: A voyage is 20 to 40 minutes and leaving abandons it, so a player whose sittings are six minutes (the commuter in Docs/LoopAtlas/personas/journeys.yaml) never finishes one.
holes.fill: The Ark docks at the location it reached when the player leaves; the next sitting sails from there, one leg at a time.

holes.q: The plan says a voyage is 3 to 6 legs and 20 to 40 minutes, but the one job the board offers since 2026-11-21 is the Crystal Run (commit 00373d12f), and its 4-cell run takes about 8 minutes to its stop and 3 more home (commit 9addc48ee, the way home at 2x). Is the Crystal Run the short job by design, or the first leg of the longer voyage?
holes.fill: The Crystal Run stays the short job (about 11 minutes, one sitting on a phone) and is the first leg the longer voyages chain, so a 20 to 40 minute voyage is 2 to 4 runs with a port between them.

phases.d: The autopilot flies the step once, then hands over the stick.

now.note: Built and merged, never run in the editor. The master unlock is on in shipped builds, so a fresh install gets every lock open and no guidance.

plan.note: The Microgame Training plan. The gate is flipped once the chain is signed off.

holes.q: No player has seen the onboarding. The first loop a stranger meets is an unlocked menu.
The Lesson teaches a ship's Time verb. Nothing yet teaches a combo or a role.
holes.fill: The Mentor's stream is ordered by the ladder of tiers: Pulse and Verb in the Lesson, the kit's first Combo after three races, the Role the first time the player enters a Mass-Space game.

holes.q: Activation is one funnel: every new player is led to a flying race. Simulated, a player who came for the Ratel's puzzle flies 62% of her arcade rounds today and all of them once the gate flips (the Honeyguide's cards open only after the chain), and leaves (D30 3 to 4%).
holes.fill: Activation has doors, each measured on its own: fly (first race finished), solve (first Ratel board played, P14), make (first painting shared, P16), crew (first match with a friend, P15). The first-login guide asks which one and spotlights it.

holes.q: Nothing says how often a new player should win their first ten rounds. Simulated against an I1 AI of strength 0.15, a non-flyer takes first in 16% of them, a commuter 32%, the teen core 37%.
holes.fill: Target: a new player takes first in at least half of their first ten rounds, read from game_completed placement in the first sittings. The I1 AI reaches it with fun, suboptimal behaviour loops (the AI complexity rule), never random mistakes.

holes.q: Activation has one door: first launch, the spotlight, a Lesson that flies a Time verb. Two of the six journeys (Mira, the night crew) arrive by invite and never pass through it, and Mira does not want to fly at all.
holes.fill: Activation starts where the player arrived: an invite starts in the inviter's party and the seat it named, and the Lesson for that seat (a crew board, a hull) runs there.

nodes.name: The quest chain

holes.q: The chain orders 4 cards. About 80 others have no order, so after the Hangar opens nothing says what to play next.
holes.fill: After the Hangar, the chain is per vessel: each hull's flower (see The vessel's flower) is its own short chain of three element games.

plan.note: A quest clears at I2, so the chain is about four to eight wins, and I3 and I4 stay the ladder's challenge after the Hangar.

build.what: A quest clears at I2, so the chain is about four to eight wins, and I3 and I4 stay the ladder's challenge after the Hangar.

Learn its kit in its games

now.note: The economy is live: the winner is paid 200, everyone else nothing; five vessels cost 4000 each. Twenty-three hulls exist; most are not priced or in the shipping list.

prop.note: Crystals get a second sink so the loop does not end with the last vessel.

holes.q: Crystals buy only vessels. When the fleet is owned the reward has no use, and the payout stops driving anything.
holes.fill: Three more sinks: refitting the Ark (hold and plates), recruiting a pilot at port, and colour sets.

holes.q: Which of the 23 hulls ship, at what price and in what order, is not decided beyond the first five.
holes.fill: Price by how many loops a hull opens: a solo hull 4000, a crew vessel 6000 because it opens a second seat for a friend.

holes.q: A daily arena player owns all seven priced vessels by day 12 to 14 and holds about 60,000 crystals nobody can spend by day 42 (simulated). P7's three sinks add about nine days. A casual or puzzle player never reaches the first vessel at all.
holes.fill: Two ends to fix. For the core: open the other hulls over the Tides (one or two per Tide), so the fleet has a new goal every six weeks, and keep P7's sinks. For the casual end: their first vessel comes from the doors they play (a solved board, a shared painting, a daily job), not only from placing.

holes.q: Today the master unlock owns every vessel, so crystals buy nothing and no playtest can measure the economy: whatever testers earn is banked and never spent.
holes.fill: A tester build that keeps the unlock for modes and the Hangar but locks vessels, so the earn-to-buy step can be watched before launch.

holes.q: Only the winner is paid. In a group of friends who beat each other, the one who wins least owns nothing new after two weeks; in the night crew journey that friend leaves on day 17 and the crew shrinks.
holes.fill: Pay a team win to every seat on the team, crew seats included, and pay a little for finishing, so a friend's fleet grows at the group's pace.

proposals.what: Use the eight tier terms (Pulse, Verb, Combo, Role, Round, Session, Arc, Era) in every design doc, ticket and review, so a problem is placed before it is argued.

proposals.what: Each ability's doc gets its loop as steps and one sentence: the feeling, and the step where it lands. The fun card asks about that step.

proposals.title: Show the role
proposals.what: The two volume numbers the scoreboard already books become one live meter, and the vessel's measured lean goes on its Hangar card.

proposals.what: A daily job, a weekly card and a six-week season, built from the living sea's tick and the studio's rebalance.

proposals.title: More to spend crystals on
proposals.what: Ark refits, recruiting pilots and colour sets, so the payout still drives something after the last vessel.

proposals.title: The vessel's flower
proposals.what: Three petals per hull, lit by clearing its Time, Charge and Mass-Space games at I3. The player's own pass through the elemental loop.

proposals.title: Set the counts
proposals.what: Cells per leg, rounds per run, matches per set, passes per round: each gets a target number and an analytics event that measures it.

proposals.what: Voyage pay is the same crystals as arcade pay, so 'the voyage ended, buy a vessel' is a real path.

proposals.what: A party shares one voyage record, and a crew vessel's empty seat is an invite.

A 20 to 40 minute voyage becomes two to four phone sittings, and a commuter stops losing hauls (100% of started voyages simulated as planned, none with chapters).

proposals.what: The first-login guide asks fly or solve. A solver's spotlight leads to the Ratel's board while the Honeyguide's AI flies, and a Honeyguide game counts for the quest chain. Simulated, it lifts a puzzle player's D30 from 3% to 94%, with P15.

proposals.title: A crew vessel in every squad
proposals.what: Every crew vessel seats at least one arena card and a voyage squad, so two people share one seat: a parent rides as the Ratel in a child's arena squad, and four friends fit three seats.

proposals.what: A finished painting pays a little and can be shared as a replay link; a liked painting is the creative player's win. The Toybox feeds the long game instead of standing beside it.

genes.is: Every combo is also an AI behaviour: one gene of the vessel's genome for one element (Docs/AI_SYSTEM/AI_PLAN.md, one AI per vessel per element). A gene names the cues that start the combo, the dials a search learns (each with the range it may try; a seed is whatever the shipped AI does today, and no dial is typed by hand after a search writes it), the moment it counts as done, and the pilot callsign whose sight leans into it. A pilot only changes what the AI goes after, never what the vessel can do. The same done-moment is the combo_completed event, so the AI and the player are measured by one count.
genes.activation: A new pilot completes the first combo listed for a vessel at least once within their first three rounds on that vessel. The Mentor teaches that combo after the Lesson (arc.activation, hole 1). combo_completed carries vessel, combo, genome, seconds and whether a person or an AI flew it, so the same number reads activation and AI coverage.

search.is: Garrett, 2026-11-21: a search tells two kinds of complexity apart, keeps one small and weights toward the other. Players get a more interesting game from vessels that switch between noticeably different behaviours, and less from a perfect AI with mistakes added.
search.cut: Bloat: a dial, cue or branch that changes nothing an onlooker can see and nothing the score shows, that only widens the search space, or that costs effectiveness. The search pays a cost for every dial and branch a genome uses, and drops a dial whose whole range moves neither the outcome nor the visible behaviour.
search.keep: Style: switching between noticeably different behaviours (different genes of the genome, or one gene flown in clearly different ways) whose effectiveness is roughly comparable. The search keeps an archive of distinct behaviours (MAP-Elites over which genes fire, how often, and when) beside the single best genome, and rewards a genome that switches between archive cells without losing effectiveness.
search.ladder: Skill comes down by weighting a genome toward the fun, less effective behaviours the archive kept, never by adding random mistakes to the best one. A behaviour that costs effectiveness but reads as a real pilot is recycled for the lower rungs (I1, I2) and for AI teammates, so the player feels they play with or against a person, not a perturbed optimiser. The top rung (I4) flies the best archive cells; every rung still switches.
search.measure: combo_completed per AI round: distinct genes used, switches between them, and each gene's effectiveness next to the genome's best. Proposed target: at I2 and above, three or more distinct genes a round with the best and third within a fifth of each other; lower rungs lean on genes up to a third less effective, not on more errors. Dials per genome is reported beside the score so bloat is visible.
